sections.heading: Flagged items in detail
paragraphs: Receivables vs. Revenue Growth: Days sales outstanding moved +11 days over 5 years while revenue compounded 5.4%. Receivables are growing faster than sales, which can flatter revenue recognition and must be watched.
CFO vs. Net Income Conversion: Operating cash flow converted 22% of reported net profit. Profit is running ahead of cash generation, which points to working-capital or accrual quality issues.
Working Capital Cycle (DSO / DIO): The cash conversion cycle absorbs 81 days of working capital. A long cycle ties up cash and makes growth expensive to fund.
Book Value Compounding: Book value per share compounded 2.3% annually. Retained earnings are not translating into balance-sheet growth.
